You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
A hospital management board decides to reallocate $800000 from its $1.2m new buildings budget to spend on cancer care. What is the opportunity cost of this decision?

options.A: a cost of $400000
options.C: the cost of healthcare for cancer patients
options.D: the loss of some new buildings

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the change in a country’s production possibility curve from XX to YY. Y food X O Y X drink What would explain this change?

options.A: Consumers chose to consume more food and less drink.
options.B: Government taxed food production and subsidised drink production.
options.C: Productivity rose in food production and fell in drink production.
options.D: There were more imports of food and more exports of drink.

questions.questionText: A factory manufactures chairs. The manufacturing process is divided into a number of tasks. What is a likely disadvantage of this division of labour?

options.A: decrease in motivation
options.D: decrease in quality of the final product

questions.questionText: Which row correctly describes the relationship between two goods implied by the value of the cross elasticity of demand? value of the cross description elasticity of demand

options.A: –2.0 weak complements
options.D: +2.0 strong complements

questions.questionText: What does consumer surplus measure?

options.A: the excess profit earned by the producer of a good
options.B: the opportunity cost to the consumer of not buying a good
options.C: the price the marginal consumer is willing to pay for a good
options.D: the consumer’s gain from purchasing a good at a price below what they are willing to pay

questions.questionText: When the price of good X is $2.00, the quantity supplied is 100000. The price elasticity of supply of good X is 0.8 in the short run and 1.4 in the long run. The price of good X increases to $2.20. What is the increase in the quantity supplied of good X between the short run and the long run?

The diagram shows the European market for diesel fuel and the original equilibrium is at M. S price 1 M G H N J D D O R T quantity Europeans want low-emission cars and therefore the demand for diesel fuel has decreased from

options.D: to D .

questions.questionText: In which situation is the demand for a product said to be price elastic?

options.A: The quantity demanded responds to a change in price.
options.B: An increase in price brings about a decrease in the quantity demanded.
options.C: An increase in price induces consumers to spend more on the product.
options.D: A decrease in price brings about an increase in revenue.

questions.questionText: Golf club membership fees in Singapore have risen as a result of restrictions on travel to cheaper golf courses in neighbouring countries and the closure of some local courses. The supply of golf club memberships is determined by the current number of courses. If the original equilibrium was at X, which point shows the result of these changes? S S S

The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for solar energy in India. The initial equilibrium point is at X. The Indian government increases the subsidy to solar energy producers. At the same time, there is a rise in the price of alternative sources of energy. What is the new equilibrium position? S price of A S solar energy S 3 D X B D C D D O quantity of solar energy

A specific tax is placed on the sale of bottles of lemonade. In the diagram, S is the supply curve before imposition of the tax and S is the supply curve after tax. t S t price S W U X D T O quantity Which distance represents the specific tax on each bottle?

options.A: UT B WT C WU D WX

questions.questionText: Demand for medical face masks exceeds supply during a disease outbreak. What is the most likely cause of this excess demand?

options.A: Some consumers do not have effective demand.
options.B: The demand for medical face masks is price inelastic in the short run.
options.C: The price of medical face masks is fixed below the equilibrium price.
options.D: The supply of medical face masks is inelastic in the short run.

Which statement correctly describes absolute advantage?

options.A: It is when a country has a higher opportunity cost in producing a good than another country.
options.B: It is when a country has a lower wage cost in producing a good than another country.
options.C: It is when the relative prices of exports of a country are greater than the relative prices of its imports.
options.D: It is when a country’s output of a good is greater per unit of resource than another country.

questions.questionText: The table shows the income and wealth of Yasmin. items $ children’s welfare benefits 1000 dividends from shares 1000 property owned 40000 savings in bank 1000 shares 2000 wages 10000 What is the value of Yasmin’s wealth?
Which group is most likely to suffer during high inflation?

options.A: borrowers
options.D: fixed wage earners

questions.questionText: Which statement explains why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping?

options.A: As prices fall, the demand for exports becomes more elastic.
options.B: As prices fall, fewer goods are imported.
options.C: As prices fall, the rate of interest will rise.
options.D: As prices fall, real wealth rises and so spending increases.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) for an economy. AS general price AS level 1 AD O real output Which changes in subsidies and indirect taxes would have caused the change from AS to AS ?

options.A: a fall in consumer expenditure across the whole period
options.B: an initial fall in consumer expenditure followed by a rise

questions.questionText: In the diagram, the intersection of AD and LRAS at point X represents the current macroeconomic equilibrium. Which point could represent the new equilibrium after the introduction of an increase in the retirement age? LRAS LRAS LRAS
The table shows data on the Japanese balance of trade in goods. exchange rate exports imports year yen/dollar $bn $bn 2016 109 635 585 2017 111 689 645 What can be concluded from this data?

options.A: The demand for Japanese exports was price inelastic.
options.B: The Japanese current account was in surplus.
options.C: The majority of Japanese imports were essential goods.
options.D: The Marshall–Lerner condition for Japan is greater than 1.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows production possibility curves for two countries, India and Japan. rice India Japan 0 200 tea Which combination of outputs would be achieved if each country specialised in the product in which it has a comparative advantage? rice tea
A country’s currency has depreciated against all the currencies of its main trading partners. How will the depreciation affect its terms of trade?

options.A: The terms of trade will improve.
options.B: The terms of trade will not change.
options.C: The terms of trade will worsen.
options.D: The terms of trade will worsen only if the depreciation causes inflation.

questions.questionText: A country with a floating exchange rate experiences a large surplus on the current account of its balance of payments. What is likely to decrease as a consequence?

options.A: the exports of capital from the country
options.B: the level of employment in the country
options.C: the prices of imports into the country
options.D: the value of the country’s currency

questions.questionText: Which measure is aimed directly at promoting international trade?

options.A: decreasing existing quotas
options.D: wage subsidy schemes during recessions

questions.questionText: What would be classified as a supply-side policy measure?

options.A: a law to reduce the power of trade unions
options.B: a reduction in the government’s fiscal deficit
options.C: an open market sale of securities
options.D: the imposition of a tariff on imported goods

questions.questionText: What is the equivalent of a country’s national debt?

options.A: the accumulated borrowing of the government
options.B: the difference between government spending and taxation
options.C: the interest paid by the government on all the money it owes
options.D: the total money owed by all households in the country

questions.questionText: A country experiences a fall in the value of exports and an increase in the value of imports of goods and services. What are the effects of these changes? balance of aggregate payments on demand goods and services

options.A: fall improve
options.D: rise worsen

questions.questionText: A government orders its central bank to buy its domestic currency on the foreign exchange markets in the belief that this will improve the balance of payments. What does this suggest?

options.A: Demand for the country’s exports is price inelastic.
options.B: The country’s Marshall–Lerner condition is greater than 1.
options.C: The government has a budget deficit.
